summary: Declaration-level refinement of the accepted U.1 packet’s remaining U.6 comparisons. Absolute K₁, determinant, transfer and computations remain imports by their existing IDs. The double-ring algebra is separated from the unresolved low-degree map of homotopy fibres and its two boundary comparisons. The coherent graded determinant receives a precisely typed π₁ comparison, using the existing Z.3 determinant and the H.4/H.5 and K.4 model interfaces. This is a complete planning pass with U.6 planned, explicit proof and supplier gaps, and no implementation claims.

nodes.title: Congruence groups of the double ring
nodes.statement: For any unital map q:A→C of associative rings, D_q=RingHom.pullback(q,q), pr and add its first and second projections, and any finite decidable index set n, entrywise add induces a multiplicative equivalence c_{q,n}:ker(GL_n(pr))≃ker(GL_n(q)). Its inverse sends g to the compatible-pair matrix (1,g), with inverse matrix (1,g⁻¹). For q:A→A/I this is the finite-rank form of GL(D,J)≃GL(A,I), J=ker pr; transport to A⊕I uses the existing U.5 double-ring equivalence.
proofSteps: A matrix with first projection 1 has entries (δ_ij,g_ij); compatibility is exactly q(g)=1. The inverse of g has the same property because coefficient maps are group homomorphisms.
Pair the identity with g and with g⁻¹ entrywise. Multiplication is componentwise, so these matrices are mutual inverses in the compatible-pair ring.
Second projection and this lift are inverse homomorphisms; unit and product identities hold entrywise. Neither surjectivity of q nor commutativity of A is used.
acceptance: The comparison uses the second projection; the first projection is identically 1 on the source.
For q=id_A, both kernels are trivial.

nodes.title: Stable double congruence comparison
nodes.statement: For a unital q:A→C, the finite-rank second-projection equivalences induce c_q:GL(D_q,ker pr)≃GL(A,ker q) of stable congruence groups, with inverse represented at every finite rank by (1,g).
proofSteps: Apply double-congruence-stabilisation to the finite second projections. Applying the finite equivalence to both sides also gives inverse compatibility.
Use finite representatives to define both stable maps. The stable equality criterion makes them well defined; the finite inverse identities make them mutually inverse.
acceptance: No passage to an unstabilised relative elementary quotient is asserted.

nodes.title: Relative elementary image under the second projection
nodes.statement: Let A be an associative unital ring, I a two-sided ideal, D=A⊕I and J=ker pr. Under c_q, the image of E(D,J) is exactly E(A,I), where each relative elementary subgroup is the normal closure of the ideal-entry elementary matrices inside its ambient stable elementary group.
proofSteps: For the forward inclusion, add sends e_ij(0,x) to e_ij(x), x∈I, and E(D) into E(A), hence sends every relative generator and elementary conjugate into E(A,I).
For the reverse inclusion, lift the conjugating h∈E(A) along the common ring section Δ:A→D and lift x∈I to (0,x)∈J. The resulting conjugate belongs to E(D,J) and maps to h e_ij(x) h⁻¹.
Products and inverses of generators give equality. Since c_q is injective, it identifies the two subgroups.
acceptance: The common section Δ is used to lift elementary conjugators. This is stronger data than an arbitrary isomorphism of nonunital ideals.

nodes.title: Algebraic relative K₁ of the double ring
nodes.statement: For any associative unital A and two-sided I, second projection induces an isomorphism a_{A,I}:K₁(D,J)≃K₁(A,I), sending the class of a double congruence matrix to the class of its second projection. Here D=A⊕I and J=ker pr.
proofSteps: Descend the stable congruence equivalence through the identified normal relative elementary subgroups. Its inverse descends because the subgroups correspond exactly.
acceptance: For split square-zero A=B⋉M this retains the ambient elementary relations; it does not identify every ambient-ring version of K₁(M).

nodes.title: Degree one of the split double fibre
nodes.statement: For D=A⊕I, pr:D→A and Δ its section, put F_D=hofib(K(pr)) at zero. Inclusion gives π₁F_D≃ker(K₁(pr):K₁(D)→K₁(A)). Combined with U.5/relative-K1-split, denote by s₁:K₁(D,J)≃π₁F_D the inverse identification, compatible with inclusion in K₁(D).
proofSteps: K(pr)K(Δ) is identity. Consequently π₂K(pr) is surjective, and the connecting homomorphism to π₁F_D is zero.
Exactness gives injectivity of π₁F_D→π₁K(D) and image the kernel of π₁K(pr). Use the absolute θ comparison and the split relative quotient theorem to identify this kernel with K₁(D,J).
acceptance: This step does not assert any unsplit ideal excision. The section is essential.

nodes.title: Degree zero of the split double fibre
nodes.statement: For the same D and F_D, inclusion gives π₀F_D≃ker(K₀(pr):K₀(D)→K₀(A))=K₀(I). Let s₀:K₀(I)≃π₀F_D be its inverse. The group operation on π₀F_D is the functorial K-space operation.
proofSteps: The section makes π₁K(pr) surjective, so the connecting map π₁K(A)→π₀F_D is zero. The exact sequence then embeds π₀F_D into π₀K(D) with image ker π₀K(pr).
Use the canonical K₀ comparison, rather than a natural product decomposition of K(D), and the existing definition of K₀(I).
acceptance: If I=0 then D=A and the fibre is contractible.

nodes.title: Double fibre comparison in degree zero
nodes.statement: Let q:A→A/I and ω:F_D→F_q be the map on based homotopy fibres induced by the square with top pr:D→A, bottom q:A→A/I, left add:D→A and right q:A→A/I, where q add=q pr. Then π₀ω:π₀F_D→π₀F_q is an isomorphism of abelian groups.
proofSteps: Apply the generic fibre-map API to the specified commuting square. Use the coherent zero-object points; if a K-space model commutes only up to homotopy, retain that homotopy in the fibre map.

Missing argument: identify components of F_q with the double-ring projective presentation defining K₀(I), including the relation imposed by loops in K(A/I). The Milnor-patching exact row alone does not prove the comparison. The exact proof obligation is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: I=A reduces to K(A)→K(0), I=0 to the identity fibre.
A square-zero ideal has K₀(I)=0; the map must detect no extra components.

nodes.title: Double fibre comparison in degree one
nodes.statement: For the same square and specified fibre map ω, π₁ω:π₁F_D→π₁F_q is an isomorphism of groups. This assertion is only about degree one; the square is not asserted to be homotopy cartesian.
proofSteps: The double-ring and split-fibre calculations specify the candidate map and its source.

Missing relative-plus argument: show every based loop in F_q comes from a lifted stable congruence matrix, and that precisely E(A,I), rather than E(A)∩GL(A,I), is killed. Record both surjectivity and injectivity as the degree-one gap; use an acyclic early supplier route for higher attaching relations.
acceptance: The smaller quotient GL(A,I)/(E(A)∩GL(A,I)) would describe only the image in absolute K₁ and is not a substitute.
For A=ℤ/4, I=(2), the source is 1+I={1,3}, of order two.

nodes.title: Classical relative K₀ as fibre components
nodes.statement: Define ε₀:K₀(I)≃π₀F_q as π₀ω composed with s₀. Its domain is the kernel in K₀(A⊕I), and its codomain is the component group of the zero-based fibre, not merely ker(K₀(A)→K₀(A/I)).
proofSteps: Compose the two specified degree-zero isomorphisms.
acceptance: For a split quotient, this becomes the kernel identification; for an arbitrary quotient the preceding boundary can contribute.

acceptance: For I=A it agrees with the absolute matrix-loop θ_A; for I=0 both groups are trivial.

nodes.title: Naturality of the relative degree zero comparison
nodes.statement: For a unital φ:A→B carrying the two-sided ideal I into J, the square ε₀ ∘ classical relative map(φ) = π₀(F_φ) ∘ ε₀ commutes. The classical source is K₀(I); F_φ is the map induced by the quotient square with the chosen coherent basepoints.
proofSteps: The double-ring map sends (a,x) to (φ(a),φ(x)) and respects pr, add and Δ. Matrix maps and the two kernel identifications are natural.

Apply the functorial fibre-map API to the resulting cube and pass to π₀. The classical map is the induced map between the kernels defining K₀(I), so the split-kernel identification and π₀ω commute with it.
acceptance: Identity and composite pair maps give the corresponding identity and composite squares.

nodes.title: The degree-one map into absolute K-theory
nodes.statement: Inclusion j_q:F_q→K(A) satisfies π₁(j_q) ε₁ = θ_A ι, where ι:K₁(A,I)→K₁(A) is the classical map and θ_A:K₁(A)≃π₁K(A) is the imported absolute comparison.
proofSteps: Fibre functoriality makes the projection square commute. On the split source, inclusion is the kernel inclusion; second projection gives the classical map ι on congruence matrices.

nodes.title: The boundary from K₁ to relative K₀
nodes.statement: Let ∂₁^W:π₁K(A/I)→π₀F_q be the homotopy boundary transported from the K-book zero-to-image path convention into the H.2 image-to-zero fibre by its path-reversal homeomorphism. The target equation is ε₀ δ_I = ∂₁^W θ_{A/I}. Here δ_I is U.5/ideal-boundary, whose image in K₀(D) is [FreePatch(a)]−n[D] for the fixed gluing convention. The formula relating ∂₁^W to H.2’s own loop-inclusion boundary, including its sign, is part of the recorded proof obligation; ε₀ remains the previously specified split-kernel comparison.
proofSteps: Missing boundary identification: represent the quotient automorphism loop by a clutched free module over the double ring and prove the component formula with this orientation.
Retain path reversal explicitly. Neither exactness of the two rows nor equality of their kernels establishes equality of connecting maps. The required clutching-to-fibre proof is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: The boundary of a class lifted from K₁(A) is zero.
Changing the gluing or fibre-path orientation must be accompanied by the corresponding sign change; the unit class still has zero boundary.

nodes.title: The boundary from K₂ to relative K₁
nodes.statement: Let β:K₂(A/I)→K₁(A,I) be the classical relative Steinberg boundary of Theorem III.5.7.1, using the T.6 conventions. Let κ_{A/I}:K₂(A/I)≃π₂K(A/I) be T.1’s plus comparison. Let ∂₂^W be the topological boundary transported by the same path-reversal convention as relative-boundary-one. The target equation is ε₁ β = ∂₂^W κ_{A/I}; its relation to H.2’s loop-inclusion orientation must be computed, not inferred from exactness. This is an equality of homomorphisms to π₁F_q.
proofSteps: Lift a Steinberg word representing a kernel element over A/I, take its elementary image over A, and regard that image modulo E(A,I) as β. This construction and its well-definedness belong to T.6.

Missing comparison: match this class with the fibre boundary of the corresponding sphere under κ, including path reversal and the central extension convention. Equality π₂=K₂ alone does not identify β.

Import the existing absolute k2-pi2 theorem and the classical exact-row portion of relative-steinberg-group. Request their representative-level normalisations from T.1:plus and T.6. The latter node also contains a separate relative π₂ comparison gap, which is not used to prove this boundary equation.
acceptance: For a split quotient, β and ∂₂ are zero.
The image is ker(K₁(A,I)→K₁(A)); identifying only this image does not prove equality of the maps.

nodes.title: Graded determinant on a free automorphism
nodes.statement: For a commutative unital ring R and g∈GL_n(R), the morphism Det^ℤ(g) of the graded line Det^ℤ(Rⁿ) acts on its determinant line by multiplication by det(g)∈Rˣ. The grade is n on every point of Spec R, and this assertion concerns morphisms rather than only Picard classes.
proofSteps: Use the projective graded determinant map API: the morphism is the induced top exterior power.

Use exteriorPower.topEquiv in the ordered standard basis and exteriorPower.map_top_eq_det_smul for the underlying free linear automorphism. The existing free determinant compatibility identifies LinearMap.det with the matrix determinant. This imports the top-exterior scalar calculation instead of reproving it.
The inverse automorphism gives the inverse coefficient, so this is a unit-valued identity and does not depend on a choice of volume element.
acceptance: For the swap of two rank-one summands over ℤ the value is −1.
The empty free module gives the unit on its determinant line.

sources.locator: Proposition 12.3, p.55; Corollary 12.17, p.59
sources.match: The symmetric monoidal determinant acts on isomorphisms by their top exterior maps and induces the determinant spectrum map. The loop calculation here follows these maps through the group-completion unit.

nodes.title: Determinant of a translated projective automorphism loop
nodes.statement: Let R be commutative and P finite projective. An automorphism α:P≃P gives a loop at [P] under the group-completion unit η:N(iso P(R))→Ω∞K(R). Translate this loop to the zero component by the inverse of η(P), using the coherent grouplike law, and write ℓ_P(α)∈π₁K(R). Then Det_R sends it to the unit corresponding to Det^ℤ(α):Aut(Det^ℤ(P))≃Rˣ. The target translation tensors with the inverse graded line, so its basepoint is (R,0).
proofSteps: The extension property for the group-completed determinant supplies a specified homotopy Det_R η ≃ N(Det^ℤ). Applying it to the isomorphism edge α identifies the image loop at Det^ℤ(P).
The determinant extension is a map of grouplike E∞ spaces, so it takes translation by η(P)⁻¹ to tensor translation by Det^ℤ(P)⁻¹.

nodes.title: The spectrum determinant on π₁
nodes.statement: For every commutative unital ring R, let d_R:π₁K(R)→Rˣ be π₁(Det_R) followed by π₁Pic^ℤ(Spec R)≃Aut((R,0))≃Rˣ, and let θ_R:K₁(R)≃π₁K(R) be the specified zero-component comparison. As group homomorphisms, d_R ∘ θ_R = det_R:K₁(R)→Rˣ. In particular d_R(θ_R([g]))=Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.det(g) for every finite matrix unit g. This promotes the exact used Z.3/ring-spectrum-det π₁ API to a node; it creates no new determinant map.
proofSteps: For a finite matrix representative g, the translated-loop lemma and free exterior calculation give d_R(ℓ(g))=det(g). The model comparison identifies ℓ(g) with θ_R([g]).
Every stable matrix has a finite representative, and every K₁ class is the image of a stable matrix in the quotient. Equality on those representatives gives equality of the two homomorphisms.
The classical determinant already descends through elementary matrices and stabilisation in U.3; these objects and their determinant are imported.

nodes.title: Coherent determinant after finite-free restriction
nodes.statement: Let R→B be a map of commutative rings with B finite free as a right R-module, with a chosen basis b. Let t:K₁(B)→K₁(R) be the classical transfer and T:K(B)→K(R) the K-space restriction-of-scalars map from the owning K-theory roadmap. Then d_R π₁(T) θ_B = det_R t. On g∈GL_n(B), this is the determinant over R of the restriction matrix in the induced basis bⁿ; no identification with a group homomorphism Bˣ→Rˣ is used without a norm theorem.
proofSteps: The imported transfer-on-π₁ comparison gives π₁(T)θ_B=θ_R t; follow it by the determinant-on-π₁ theorem.
The classical finite-free transfer is defined by the restriction matrix, so its determinant is the displayed value. Basis changes conjugate that matrix and leave its determinant unchanged.
